subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` become OpenClaw’s supported operator escape hatch for early provider recovery, or should recovery instead be owned by Doctor, an in-product Fix surface, or automatic probing?
rationale: The branch is a narrow implementation, but selecting a permanent public command that mutates persisted provider availability—and deciding whether terminal-only recovery is acceptable—requires product and ownership intent.

options.title: Adopt the explicit reset
options.body: Confirm the profile-scoped command as the supported opt-in escape hatch after redacted runtime evidence proves the complete recovery flow.

options.title: Use guided recovery instead
options.body: Pause this command and place the action behind Doctor or an in-product recovery surface so affected users do not need to edit state or infer a CLI workflow.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close this PR if maintainer direction is to handle early recovery only through runtime probing and fallback policy rather than manual state mutation.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit reset
recommendation.body: Confirm the profile-scoped command as the supported opt-in escape hatch after redacted runtime evidence proves the complete recovery flow.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile invariant work with merger responsibility for related cooldown-state corrections.
